description: An advanced, real-time health monitoring and emergency response system tailored for astronauts in space exploration. The platform integrates cloud-based telemetry data (via Firebase) with a context-aware Gemini AI assistant to track critical vitals (HR, SpO2, Temp), trigger instant emergency protocols, and provide bidirectional multi-domain support, ensuring crew safety and mission resilience in zero-gravity environments.
summary:
Space Doctor is an autonomous health monitoring platform for astronauts on long-duration missions, where contact with Earth may be delayed or unavailable.

It continuously tracks vital signs, psychological state, spacecraft environment, and behavioral patterns, and combines them to detect early warning signs that single measurements would miss. A transparent rules engine, linked to a documented medical knowledge base, classifies severity (self-manage or contact Earth immediately) and provides step-by-step guidance. Every threshold is traceable to its source.

An AI assistant answers health questions in plain language and generates medical reports for crew follow-up and ground teams.

Our goal: protect astronaut health and enable safer missions to Mars.
details:
Space Doctor is a web-based health and wellbeing monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions. It brings physical health and mental health into one dashboard, so warning signs are caught early, even when help from Earth is delayed.

The problem: On missions to the Moon and Mars, crews face space radiation, a sealed environment, and months of isolation. Physical readings and psychological wellbeing are usually tracked separately, so early signs of trouble in either one are easy to miss.

How it works: The astronaut logs in with a smart wristband ID and gets a live dashboard with three groups of indicators: space radiation sensors, closed-environment and air-quality readings, and isolation and wellbeing indicators. When a reading moves outside its configured threshold, the system raises a live medical alert. A built-in health assistant gives guidance from a local medical knowledge base. For mental health and daily routine, the crew-support tools include daily mood, motivation and stress tracking, an astronaut journal, sleep and circadian-rhythm logging, a light-exposure scheduler with a session timer, a workload and performance tracker, a space-gardening activity log, coping tips for isolation, a post-mission reintegration plan, and a HERA/CHAPEA analog-mission simulation log. Every entry is saved to the astronaut's profile in Firebase, and a NASA research sample (User_1) can be imported to test the system.

Benefits and intended impact: One view of body and mind lets the crew and the mission support team notice changes sooner. Astronauts can keep healthy routines, sleep and social contact, and mission teams get a documented history of crew wellbeing to review over time. The goal is safer and more resilient crews on missions where help is far away.

Tools and software: HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web app, JSON files for data, Firebase for cloud data storage, Visual Studio Code as the code editor, and GitHub Pages for hosting. Public NASA resources and analog-mission information (HERA, CHAPEA) guided the design.

What makes it creative: most monitoring tools focus on the body only. Space Doctor treats mental wellbeing as equally important and adds practical tools against monotony, such as space gardening activities and light-exposure scheduling.

Factors our team considered: safety and honesty. Alert thresholds are experimental and adjustable, mood and behavior scores are self-reported and not diagnostic, the HERA/CHAPEA log is for documentation and simulation only, and all medical decisions are left to the mission medical team.
